title: Beachhead Strategy
equation: Beachhead Strength = (Segment Share + Reference Density + Whole-Product Fit) ÷ 3
hook: Trying to sell to everyone is how you end up selling to no one.
statement: Win one narrow segment completely before you try to expand.
explainer: A small market you own gives you a base, loyal customers, and references. Pick a niche close enough to the next one that those references carry over when you expand.
sop: Define a segment small enough to actually own.
Tailor your product, price, and marketing only to them.
Push for majority share in that segment.
Use their references to enter the next segment.
equation_example: Score each 1 to 10. Segment Share 6, Reference Density 4, Whole-Product Fit 7. (6 + 4 + 7) ÷ 3 = 5.7. Higher means you're close to owning your niche. Lower means you're still spread thin, even inside your own beachhead.
question: Describe a segment small enough that you could win most of it in the next year.
closing_statement: Owning a small market beats renting a big one.
caption:
Principle Nº 292: Beachhead Strategy

Trying to sell to everyone is how you end up selling to no one.

Win one narrow segment completely before you try to expand.

Your turn: Describe a segment small enough that you could win most of it in the next year.
